scope: Submission edges from ANV execbuffer to the execlists submit registers on Alder Lake-S 8086:4680; source and host-fixture evidence only, never GPU execution
how_to_read: Each edge names the caller, the callee and the native code that actually runs. classification is one of: verified-source (implementation read and consistent), fixture-covered (executed by a host fixture, model primitives noted), defect-pending (a concrete defect that still needs a fix), unverified (implementation not read to the end or only the target can answer).

verified_edges.edge: i915 register mapping -> IOKit kernel mapping cache attribute
anchors: drm: drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/intel_uncore.c:2361 uncore->regs = ioremap(phys_addr, mmio_size)
freebsd: sys/compat/linuxkpi/common/include/linux/io.h:424-425 ioremap() -> _ioremap_attr(addr, size, VM_MEMATTR_DEVICE)
port: bsdcompat/include/machine/vm.h:3,10 VM_MEMATTR_UNCACHEABLE 0x00 and VM_MEMATTR_DEVICE == VM_MEMATTR_UNCACHEABLE
port: bsdcompat/src/nmx_page.c:654-669 pmap_mapdev_attr -> nmx_xnu_map_phys(pa, size, mode, &d->handle)
port: bsdcompat/include/nmx_xnu.h:17 NMX_CACHE_UC 0x00
port: xnu/nmx_vm.cpp:21-28 cache_option(): NMX_CACHE_UC -> kIOMapInhibitCache
verified_edges.contract: This port redefines the FreeBSD VM_MEMATTR_* values as x86 PAT encodings, so VM_MEMATTR_UNCACHEABLE(0x00)/WRITE_COMBINING(0x01)/WRITE_THROUGH(0x04)/WRITE_BACK(0x06) equal NMX_CACHE_UC/WC/WT/WB. Plain ioremap() therefore lands on VM_MEMATTR_DEVICE == UNCACHEABLE == NMX_CACHE_UC and the kernel mapping is created with kIOMapInhibitCache. The enumerations are not silently mismatched, and MMIO is not a write-back mapping.

verified_edges.edge: readl()/writel() used for ELSP, forcewake and CSB registers
anchors: freebsd: sys/compat/linuxkpi/common/include/linux/io.h:184-205 readl = le32toh(__raw_readl(addr)), writel = __raw_writel(htole32(v), addr)
freebsd: sys/compat/linuxkpi/common/include/linux/io.h:105-116 __raw_readl/__raw_writel are volatile 32-bit loads/stores
verified_edges.contract: On x86 the le32toh/htole32 pair is the identity, so readl/writel are plain 32-bit uncached loads/stores with the register width the hardware expects, and neither carries an implicit fence. That matches upstream Linux x86, where drivers must order explicitly.

anchors: port: bsdcompat/include/machine/atomic.h:73-75 mb = mfence, rmb = lfence, wmb = sfence
freebsd: sys/compat/linuxkpi/common/include/linux/io.h:134 mmiowb() = barrier()
port: bsdcompat/include/machine/bus.h:17 bus_space_barrier = compiler barrier
verified_edges.contract: wmb() is SFENCE, which serialises prior write-back/write-combining/write-through stores before a later uncached register write; mb() is MFENCE. mmiowb() and bus_space_barrier are compiler barriers, exactly as Linux x86 defines mmiowb(). No barrier used by the submit path is weaker than its upstream x86 counterpart.

anchors: drm: drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/intel_execlists_submission.c:3554-3566 HAS_LOGICAL_RING_ELSQ selects submit_reg = RING_EXECLIST_SQ_CONTENTS and ctrl_reg = RING_EXECLIST_CONTROL, and derives engine->fw_domain from the control register write domain

drm: drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_pci.c:674-680 adl_s_info is GEN12_FEATURES; that set carries .has_logical_ring_elsq = 1 (i915_pci.c:709) and .has_llc = 1 (i915_pci.c:707), and the platform sets .dma_mask_size = 39
drm: gt/intel_execlists_submission.c:719-728 write_desc: with ctrl_reg, low word at submit_reg + port*2 and high word at +1; without it, high word then low word to submit_reg
drm: gt/intel_execlists_submission.c:901-935 execlists_submit_ports writes one descriptor per pending port and then writel(EL_CTRL_LOAD, ctrl_reg)
verified_edges.contract: Alder Lake-S is GEN12_FEATURES with has_logical_ring_elsq set, so submission is two 32-bit writes per port into the submit-queue contents followed by an explicit EL_CTRL_LOAD control write, under the forcewake domain that write needs (taken at gt/intel_execlists_submission.c:513-514). On this port both register types are uncached mappings, so the descriptor pair and the load write reach the device in program order without an extra fence.

verified_edges.edge: context image store -> wmb() -> uncached ELSP descriptor write
anchors: drm: gt/intel_execlists_submission.c:700-713 writes ce->lrc_reg_state[CTX_RING_TAIL] and calls wmb() with a comment that the WC context write may not reach the HW before the UC register write

drm: i915_pci.c:674-680 adl_s_info = GEN12_FEATURES, which sets .has_llc = 1 (i915_pci.c:707); intel_gt_coherent_map_type therefore selects the write-back map type when the object is not always_coherent
port: machine/atomic.h:75 wmb() = sfence
port: bsdcompat/src/nmx_page.c:687-692 the port records cache attributes on pages and states system memory stays cached in the kernel's own view
verified_edges.contract: SFENCE flushes write-combining buffers and orders earlier stores, so the context image is published before the descriptor that names it. The remaining dependency is that a write-back context image is actually coherent to the GPU. For ADL-S that rests on the shared LLC, which is a device feature (has_llc = 1) and not a PCIe snooping property, and which software cannot demonstrate without the part.
verified_edges.classification: verified-source; the coherence half is target-only

verified_edges.edge: ANV syncobjs -> EXECBUFFER2 fence array -> i915 in-fence waits
anchors: mesa: src/intel/vulkan/i915/anv_batch_chain.c:565-580 setup_execbuf_fence_params: with timeline values it adds DRM_I915_GEM_EXECBUFFER_EXT_TIMELINE_FENCES; otherwise it sets I915_EXEC_FENCE_ARRAY with num_cliprects = syncobj_count and cliprects_ptr = syncobjs
drm: gem/i915_gem_execbuffer.c:2947 add_fence_array parses the array only when I915_EXEC_FENCE_ARRAY is set
drm: gem/i915_gem_execbuffer.c:3258-3301 eb_fences_add awaits the context syncobj, the submit fence and await_fence_array(rq), then creates the out fence with sync_file_create
verified_edges.contract: A VkFence submission has no timeline values, so it takes the fence-array path: a packed array of drm_i915_exec_fence entries, awaited against one request before submission. The timeline extension is not used on the probe's path, which is why the completion fixture's ordinary-syncobj case is the relevant one.

verified_edges.edge: execbuf request creation and in-fence attachment order
anchors: drm: gem/i915_gem_execbuffer.c:3320-3364 eb_requests_create creates one request per batch order and attaches the in fences only to the request whose batch order is the first submitted (i + 1 == eb->num_batches)
drm: gem/i915_gem_execbuffer.c:3142 eb_requests_add and :3510 the error path that adds requests back
verified_edges.contract: For a single-batch submit the in fences are attached to the only request, so a wait registered there gates the same request the ELSP descriptor names. The multi-batch case relies on implicit ordering between the batches rather than on repeated fence attachment, which is i915's design and unchanged by the port.

unresolved_edges.edge: intel_uncore_forcewake_get/put ACK polling around the EL_CTRL_LOAD write
unresolved_edges.why: The ACK registers and their settling time are hardware behaviour. Software only shows the wait is bounded and uses the port's monotonic clock; whether the ACK actually asserts on this part cannot be shown from source.
unresolved_edges.proves: target run with a bounded forcewake wait and CSB progress

unresolved_edges.edge: intel_ring_begin/ring space accounting for the RCS0 batch, including wrap
unresolved_edges.why: Not read to the end for this pinned i915 revision; the ring is a GEM internal object whose pages come through the same allocator reviewed for T2, but the wrap and tail arithmetic has not been traced against the port's page ordering.
unresolved_edges.proves: source trace plus a host fixture over intel_ring_begin/advance/wrap

unresolved_edges.edge: HWSP and context GGTT offsets the descriptor names, versus the addresses the completion path reads
unresolved_edges.why: Belongs to T3: the vma node offset, the GGTT PTE for that offset and the hwsp_offset used by the breadcrumb must agree. Not yet traced end to end.
unresolved_edges.proves: source trace of i915_vma_pin/GGTT insert plus hwsp_offset, then a target run
